T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural yen revaluation, GPIF domestic pivot, potential USD/JPY move to 142–146

**Synopsis:**
Six weeks after the yen hit a 40-year low (~163.99/USD), market sentiment is decisively shifting. A convergence of forces — BOJ rate hike expectations (97% probability of +25bps in September, with a 50bps shock scenario being discussed), U.S.-Japan coordinated FX intervention, accelerating capital repatriation by Japanese institutions (including GPIF), and carry trade unwinding — is squeezing yen shorts. Citi flow data confirms a flip from net bearish to net bullish positioning. On the U.S. side, Fed Governor Waller's dovish commentary has trimmed rate hike expectations, narrowing the USD/JPY rate differential. JPMorgan estimates ~¥17 trillion in accumulated yen shorts could unwind, pushing USD/JPY to 142–146. The article frames the yen's turning point as structural, not merely tactical.
